# .nvmrc how to use

`.nvmrc` is a configuration file for Node Version Manager (NVM), which specifies a version of Node.js in a specific project or directory.You can use `.nvmrc`： by following steps

1. Create `.nvmrc` file：in the project or directory to create a file named `.nvmrc` and write the required Node.js version in the file.For example, you can write `14.18.2` in the `.nvmrc` file to specify version 14.18.2 using Node.js.

2. Use the specified version of Node.js：to enter the project or directory in the terminal and execute the `nvm use` command, NVM will automatically read the version number specified in the `.nvmrc` file and switch to Node.js in that version.For example, when executing the `nvm use` command, the terminal will show output： similar to the following

    ```bash
    Found '.nvmrc' with version <14.18.2>
    Now using node v14.18.2 (npm v6.14.15)
    ```

   This means that NVM has been switched to the version of Node.js specified in the `.nvmrc` file.

3. Other NVM commands：, in addition to `nvm use` command, can also use other NVM commands to manage and toggle Node.js.For example, the `nvm install` command is used to install the specified version of Node.js, the `nvm ls` command is used to list installed versions of Node.js, the `nvm alias` command is used to create alias, etc.

Note that the `.nvmrc` file is for specific items or directories, different items or directories can have different `.nvmrc` files to specify different versions of Node.js.
